newsitem.title: GERMANY: German BDI head supports Toyota in EMU debate.
newsitem.headline: German BDI head supports Toyota in EMU debate.

text.p: Hans Peter Stihl, head of the German Federation of Chambers of Commerce, expressed support for Toyota Motor Corp's decision to make future investment in Britain dependent on participation in European monetary union.
"The advantages of EMU can only be used by those countries that participate," Stihl said in an interview with the Handelsblatt newspaper due for publication on Monday.
Toyota president Hiroshi Okuda last week stirred a hornets' nest by saying his company would build future factories on the continent if Britain decides not to join EMU.
Stihl said those that remain outside EMU cannot benefit from the greater security of planning and calculation it will provide.
If Britain does not join, companies located there will still have to deal with and hedge against currency fluctuations, he said.
"These costs will be eliminated for companies in the euro-zone," he said, adding he was sure that Britain would soon see the advantages of joining a stable common currency.
"If the United Kingdom joins, that would be entirely in our interest," he said.
